paragraphs: In this Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended June 30, 2026 (this "Annual Report"), "Applied" refers to Applied Industrial Technologies, Inc., an Ohio corporation. References to "we," "us," "our," and "the Company" refer to Applied and its subsidiaries. Headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, Applied and its predecessor companies have engaged in business since 1923. Applied operates on a fiscal year ending June 30.

We are a leading value-added distributor and technical solutions provider of industrial motion, fluid power, flow control, automation technologies and related maintenance supplies. Through our comprehensive network of approximately 6,900 employee associates and approximately 580 facilities including service center, fluid power, flow control, and automation operations, as well as repair shops and distribution centers, we offer a selection of more than 9.4 million stock keeping units with a focus on industrial bearings, power transmission products, fluid power components and systems, specialty flow control, and advanced factory automation solutions, as well as general maintenance products. Our customers use our products and services for both Maintenance, Repair, and Operations ("MRO"), Original Equipment Manufacturing ("OEM"), and new system install applications across a variety of end markets primarily in North America, as well as Australia, New Zealand, and Singapore.
Our internet address is www.applied.com. The following documents are available free of charge via hyperlink from the investor relations area of our website:

•Applied's Annual Report on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K, and amendments to those reports, together with Section 16 insider beneficial stock ownership reports - these documents are posted as soon as reasonably practicable after they are electronically filed with, or furnished to, the Securities and Exchange Commission;
•Applied's Board of Directors (our "Board" or "Board of Directors") Governance Principles and Practices;
•Applied's Director Independence Standards; •Applied's Sustainability Report; and
•Charters for the Audit, Corporate Governance & Sustainability, and Executive Organization & Compensation Committees of Applied's Board of Directors.
The information available via hyperlink from our website is not incorporated into this Annual Report defined above.

Information regarding current developments in our business can be found in Item 7 of this Annual Report defined above under the caption "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations." This information is incorporated here by reference.

We serve virtually all industrial markets that require technical expertise and service as our products and solutions are directly tied to companies' production processes, efficiency initiatives, and most critical operating assets. While our business has evolved with a broader portfolio of solutions and entrance into new markets in recent years, our core remains primarily focused on connecting world-class industrial products and technologies from leading suppliers to our customers' most critical operating assets. As such, we are integral to our customers' supply chains considering the direct exposure our solutions have on our customers' core production equipment and plant capabilities, where high cost of failure, product specification, and system complexity require premier local service and inventory availability, application expertise, and aftermarket support. While we compete with other distributors and service providers offering products and solutions addressing the industrial supply chain, we believe our industry position and value proposition benefits from relative advantages tied to the following key attributes:
1) Deep technical expertise in providing solutions to critical motion control systems and related service offerings;
2) Leading positions in engineered fluid power and flow control solutions;
3) Advanced capabilities and an established footprint across advanced automation solutions;
4) Broad in-stock product offering, local inventory availability, and repair capabilities;

In addition to other information set forth in this report, you should carefully consider the following risk factors that could materially affect our business, financial condition, or results of operations and that could make an investment in Applied more speculative or risky. Certain risks are discussed in more detail in Item 7 under the caption "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations." This information is incorporated here by reference. Because of the risk factors discussed herein, past financial performance should not be considered a reliable indicator of future performance and historical trends should not be used to anticipate results or trends in future periods. For more information, see "Cautionary Statements" in Item 7.

Our business depends heavily on the operating levels of our customers and the factors that affect them, including general economic conditions. If our customers reduce their operating levels, we may experience pricing pressures, difficulty in managing inventory, challenges in forecasting, and other adverse effects. The markets for our products and services are subject to conditions or events that affect the demand for goods and materials that our customers produce. Consequently, demand for our products and services has been and will continue to be influenced by most of the same factors that affect demand for and production of customers' goods and materials.

When customers or prospective customers reduce production levels because of lower demand, increased supply, higher costs, supply chain or labor market disruptions, changes in interest rates, tight credit conditions, unfavorable currency exchange rates, governmental regulations or adverse trade policies, foreign competition, other competitive disadvantage, offshoring of production, geopolitical instability, or other reasons, their need for our products and services diminishes. Selling prices and terms of sale come under pressure, adversely affecting the profitability and the durability of customer relationships, and credit losses may increase. Inventory management becomes more difficult in times of economic uncertainty. Volatile economic and credit conditions also make it more difficult for us, as well as our customers and suppliers, to forecast and plan future business activities.

If our customers become unable or unwilling to pay amounts owed to us under unsecured trade credit arrangements it could materially and adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations. We extend unsecured trade credit to a broad range of customers across many industries. If our customers become financially distressed and experience deterioration in their cash flow or operating and financial performance due to economic downturns, competitive pressures, or reduced demand for their products, they may not be able to make scheduled payments, or may delay payment, of amounts due to us.

Supply chain disruptions could hinder our ability to meet demand, resulting in increased costs, or force us to find alternative suppliers which may be difficult to identify or more expensive to engage, thereby adversely affecting our results of operations, financial condition, and reputation. Our supply chain, including transportation availability, staffing, and cost, could be disrupted by natural or human-induced events or conditions, such as power or telecommunications outages; security incidents; terrorist attacks; war; other geopolitical events; public health crises; earthquakes; extreme weather events; fire; flood; other natural disasters; transportation disruption; labor actions, including strikes; raw materials shortages; financial problems or insolvency; trade regulations or actions; inadequate manufacturing capacity or utilization to meet demand; or other reasons beyond our control. These supply chain disruptions may result in increased costs which we may be unable to pass along to customers. In addition, if these disruptions cause us to look for acceptable alternative sources of products, they may cost more. These potential
impairments to our ability to meet customer demand could result in lost sales, increased costs, reduced profitability, and damage to our reputation.

paragraphs: We are a leading value-added distributor and technical solutions provider of industrial motion, fluid power, flow control, automation technologies and related maintenance supplies. Our leading brands, specialized services, and comprehensive knowledge serve Maintenance, Repair & Operations ("MRO") and Original Equipment Manufacturer ("OEM") end users in virtually all industrial markets through our multi-channel capabilities that provide choice, convenience, and expertise. We have a long tradition of growth dating back to 1923, the year our business was founded in Cleveland, Ohio. During 2026, business was conducted primarily in North America, as well as, Australia, New Zealand, and Singapore from 580 facilities.

The following is Management's Discussion and Analysis of significant factors that have affected our financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows during the periods included in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets, statements of consolidated income, consolidated comprehensive income and consolidated cash flows in Item 8 under the caption "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data." When reviewing the discussion and analysis set forth, please note that a significant number of SKUs ("Stock Keeping Units") we sell, or the products we sell in our Engineered Solutions segment, in any given period were not sold in the comparable period of the prior year, resulting in the inability to quantify certain commonly used comparative metrics analyzing sales, such as changes due to volumes, product mix and price.

Our 2026 consolidated sales were $5.0 billion, an increase of $403.3 million or 8.8% compared to the prior year, with acquisitions contributing to sales growth by $142.2 million or 3.1% and favorable foreign currency translation of $15.9 million increasing sales by 0.3%. Excluding the impact of businesses acquired and foreign currency translation, sales increased $245.2 million or 5.4% during the year due to higher volumes of approximately $136.2 million and the remainder from positive price contribution. The Company generated operating income of $549.5 million, or operating margin of 11.1% of sales for the year ended June 30, 2026, compared to operating income of $498.5 million, or operating margin of 10.9% of sales in the prior year. The Company generated net income of $414.5 million and $393.0 million during the years ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. Our diluted earnings per share was $10.95 in 2026 compared to $10.12 in 2025.

Shareholders' equity was $1,861.7 million at June 30, 2026 compared to $1,844.5 million at June 30, 2025. Working capital decreased $255.0 million from June 30, 2025 to $966.3 million at June 30, 2026. The current ratio was 2.6 to 1 and 3.3 to 1 at June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Applied monitors several economic indices that are key indicators for industrial economic activity in the United States. These include the Manufacturing Industrial Production ("MIP") and Manufacturing Capacity Utilization ("MCU") indices published by the Federal Reserve Board and the Purchasing Managers Index ("PMI") published by the Institute for Supply Management ("ISM"). Historically, our performance correlates well with the MCU, which measures productivity and calculates a ratio of actual manufacturing output versus potential full capacity output. When manufacturing plants are running at a high rate of capacity, they tend to wear out machinery more frequently and require replacement parts.

The MCU and PMI indices increased since June 2025, while the MIP index decreased slightly over the fiscal year. The ISM PMI registered 53.3 in June 2026, an increase from the June 2025 reading of 49.0. A reading above 50 generally indicates expansion in the U.S. manufacturing sector. 本年度截至2026年6月30日之10-K年度報告（以下稱「本年度報告」），其中「Applied」指Applied Industrial Technologies, Inc.，為Ohio州公司。提及「我們」、「我們」、「我們」及「本公司」均指Applied及其子公司。總部設於Ohio州Cleveland市，Applied及其前身公司自1923年起從事商業活動。Applied採用截至6月30日為止之會計年度。

我們為工業運動、流體動力、流量控制、自動化技術及相關維護用品之領導性附加價值經銷商與技術解決方案供應商。透過我們約6,900名員工及約580處設施，包括服務中心、流體動力、流量控制與自動化作業，以及維修工廠與配送中心之完整網路，我們提供超過940萬個庫存單位之選擇，重點為工業軸承、動力傳輸產品、流體動力零組件與系統、專業流量控制及先進工廠自動化解決方案，以及一般維護用品。我們客戶使用我們產品與服務於維護、維修與運作（「MRO」）、原廠設備製造（「OEM」）及新系統安裝應用，跨多種終端市場，主要為北美地區，以及澳洲、紐西蘭與新加坡。
我們的網站網址為www.applied.com。以下文件可透過網站投資人關係區之超連結免費取得：
•Applied之10-K年度報告、季報（10-Q）、現況報告（8-K）及對這些報告之修正，以及第16條內線人士受益股權報告－這些文件在電子檔提交至，或提供給證券交易委員會（Securities and Exchange Commission）後盡速張貼；
•Applied之董事會（稱為「董事會」或「董事會」）治理原則與實務；
•Applied之董事獨立性標準；•Applied之永續發展報告；以及
•Applied之董事會審計、企業治理與永續發展、以及執行長組織與薪酬委員會章程。
透過網站網址之超連結取得之資訊未納入上述之年度報告中。
有關本公司業務目前發展情況之資訊，請參閱本年度報告之第 7 項，其定義如上所述，標題為『管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析』。此資訊 hereby 並入本處引用。

我們服務幾乎所有需要技術專業與服務之工業市場，因為我們的產品與解決方案與公司的生產流程、效率計畫及最重要的運營資產直接相關。雖然本公司業務近年來已拓展至更廣泛的解決方案與新市場，但我們的核心仍主要聚焦於將世界級工業產品與技術從領導供應商連接至客戶最重要的運營資產。因此，我們在客戶供應鏈中扮演關鍵角色，考量我們的解決方案對客戶核心生產設備與工廠能力有直接影響，而高失敗成本、產品規格與系統複雜性則需要優質的本地服務與存貨可得性、應用專業知識與後市場支援。雖然我們與其他提供工業供應鏈產品與解決方案的經銷商與服務供應商競爭，但我們相信本公司在產業中的地位與價值主張，受益於以下關鍵特質：
1) 在提供關鍵運動控制系統解決方案與相關服務方面擁有深厚的技術專業知識；
2) 在工程流體動力與流量控制解決方案方面處於領導地位；
3) 在先進自動化解決方案方面擁有先進的能力與已建立的據點；
4) 擁有廣泛的現貨產品組合、本地存貨可得性與維修能力；

本公司為工業運動、液壓、流量控制、自動化技術及相關維護用品的領導性附加價值經銷商與技術解決方案供應商。我們的領導品牌、專業服務與全面知識，透過多渠道能力，為幾乎所有工業市場的維護、維修與運作（"MRO"）及原廠設備製造商（"OEM"）終端用戶提供選擇、便利與專業。本公司自1923年在俄亥俄州克里夫蘭市成立以來，便有長久的成長傳統。2026年度，業務主要在北美地區進行，同時也在澳洲、紐西蘭與新加坡的580個設施進行。

以下為管理層對影響我們財務狀況、營運成果與現金流的重大因素之討論與分析，內容包含於附屬財務報表中之合併資產負債表、合併損益表、合併綜合損益表與合併現金流表。在審閱此討論與分析時，請注意我們在任一時期所銷售的SKUs（"Stock Keeping Units"）或Engineered Solutions分部所銷售的產品，與前一年同期相比，有許多並未銷售，導致無法量化常見的銷售比較指標，例如銷售量變動、產品組合與價格變動。

本公司 2026 年合併營業收入為 5.0 十億美元，較前一年增加 403.3 百萬美元或 8.8%，其中併購業務貢獻營業收入增加 142.2 百萬美元或 3.1%，有利的外幣兌換變動增加營業收入 15.9 百萬美元或 0.3%。扣除併購業務及外幣兌換變動的影響，因營業收入增加約 136.2 百萬美元的銷售量提高，以及其餘部分來自正向價格貢獻，故全年營業收入增加 245.2 百萬美元或 5.4%。本公司全年營業收入為 549.5 百萬美元，營業毛利率為銷售收入的 11.1%，較前一年營業收入為 498.5 百萬美元，營業毛利率為銷售收入的 10.9%。本公司全年淨收入為 414.5 百萬美元，及 393.0 百萬美元，分別為 2026 年及 2025 年 6 月 30 日結算年度。本公司 2026 年稀釋每股盈餘為 10.95 美元，較 2025 年的 10.12 美元為高。
2026 年 6 月 30 日，股東權益為 1,861.7 百萬美元，較 2025 年 6 月 30 日的 1,844.5 百萬美元為高。營運資金較 2025 年 6 月 30 日減少 255.0 百萬美元，為 966.3 百萬美元。2026 年 6 月 30 日的流動比率為 2.6：1，2025 年 6 月 30 日為 3.3：1。

本公司監測多項經濟指標，這些指標為美國工業經濟活動的關鍵指標。這些指標包括由聯邦儲備理事會發布的製造業工業生產（"MIP"）與製造業裝置利用率（"MCU"）指數，以及由供應管理協會（"ISM"）發布的採購經理指數（"PMI"）。歷史資料顯示，本公司表現與MCU指數有良好的關聯性，該指數衡量生產力並計算實際製造業產出與潛在滿載產能產出的比率。當製造業廠房運作在高裝置利用率時，通常會更頻繁地磨損機械，並需要更換零件。
自2025年6月以來，MCU與PMI指數均有所上升，而MIP指數則在財年期間略有下降。2026年6月的ISM PMI為53.3，較2025年6月的49.0有所上升。指數大於50通常表示美國製造業部門處於擴張狀態。最近一個財季的指數，以及前一年財年終與前一個財季終的指數如下：

除本報告中所載之其他資訊外，您應謹慎考量下列風險因素，這些因素可能重大影響本公司業務、財務狀況或營運結果，並可能使投資本公司變得更具規避性或風險性。某些風險在第7項「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」下有更詳細說明。此資訊已於 herein 透過引用方式納入。由於 herein 所述之風險因素，過去財務表現不應視為未來表現之可靠指標，歷史趨勢亦不應用以預測未來期間之結果或趨勢。如需更多資訊，請參閱第7項之「警示陳述」。
本公司業務嚴重依賴客戶之營運水準及影響其營運之因素，包括總體經濟狀況。若客戶降低其營運水準，我們可能面臨價格壓力、難以管理存貨、預測困難，以及其他不利影響。我們產品與服務之市場受影響客戶所生產商品與材料之需求之條件或事件所影響。因此，我們產品與服務之需求已並將持續受到影響客戶商品與材料之需求與生產之相同因素所影響。

當客戶或潛在客戶因需求降低、供給增加、成本提高、供應鏈或勞動市場中斷、利率變動、信貸條件緊縮、不利匯率、政府規範或不利貿易政策、外國競爭、其他競爭劣勢、生產外包、地緣政治不穩定或其他原因而降低生產水準時，其對我們產品與服務之需求將減少。銷售價格與銷售條件將面臨壓力，不利影響客戶關係之利潤率與持續性，並可能增加信貸損失。在經濟不確定時期，存貨管理將變得更加困難。波動之經濟與信貸條件亦使我們、客戶與供應商更難預測與規劃未來業務活動。
若客戶無法或不願根據無擔保貿易信貸安排支付所欠本公司之金額，將可能重大且不利影響本公司之財務狀況與營運結果。本公司向廣泛產業之客戶提供無擔保貿易信貸。若客戶因經濟衰退、競爭壓力或其產品需求降低而陷入財務困境，並經歷現金流或營運與財務表現惡化，其可能無法按時支付，或延後支付所欠本公司之金額。

供應鏈中斷可能妨礙我們滿足需求之能力，導致成本增加，或迫使我們尋找替代供應商，而這些供應商可能難以尋找或更昂貴，從而不利影響我們之營運結果、財務狀況與聲譽。我們之供應鏈，包括運輸可用性、人力與成本，可能因自然或人為事件或條件而中斷，例如電力或電信中斷；安全事件；恐怖攻擊；戰爭；其他地緣政治事件；公共衛生危機；地震；極端天氣事件；火災；洪水；其他自然災害；運輸中斷；勞動行動，包括罷工；原材料短缺；財務問題或破產；貿易規範或行動；製造能力或利用率不足以滿足需求；或其他超出我們控制範圍之原因。這些供應鏈中斷可能導致成本增加，而我們可能無法將這些成本轉嫁給客戶。此外，若這些中斷使我們尋找可接受之替代產品來源，這些來源可能更昂貴。這些潛在
對我們滿足客戶需求能力之影響可能導致銷售損失、成本增加、利潤率下降，並損害我們之聲譽。
